question: What is the primary administrative level responsible for primary health care facilities in Nigeria?
explanation: Primary health care services are primarily managed and supervised at the grassroots by the Local Government Health Department. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is primary health care considered the foundation of the national health system?

options.A: It is the first point of contact for individuals and communities.
options.B: It handles all complex surgical procedures in the country.
options.C: It only provides care for emergency trauma cases.
options.D: It is fully funded by international donor agencies only.

explanation: As the initial entry point into the health system, primary care addresses routine health needs close to the population. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which facility represents the most basic and decentralized unit in the primary health care structure?
explanation: Health posts are established in remote or sparsely populated areas to serve as the absolute first line of basic contact. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of having a tiered structure of primary health facilities?

options.A: To match the complexity of health services with community population needs
options.B: To restrict rural dwellers from ever accessing advanced doctors
options.C: To separate maternal care completely from general medical care
options.D: To ensure all facilities have equal numbers of surgical theaters

explanation: Different tiers allow basic promotional services to stay close to homes while advanced care clusters in larger centres. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is the typical population range served by a standard health post?
explanation: Health posts are designed for small, scattered rural communities with low population density. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h3)

question: A community health worker stationed at a remote health post manages a child with severe dehydration from watery diarrhea. What immediate action should be taken?

options.A: Send the child home without treatment until market day
options.C: Administer oral rehydration salts and arrange prompt transfer upward
options.D: Admit the child for major abdominal surgery at the health post

explanation: Health posts lack the capacity for severe cases, requiring basic stabilization followed by immediate referral to a higher facility. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which service is a standard primary health centre expected to provide on a continuous twenty-four-hour basis?
explanation: Labor can begin at any hour, making round-the-clock maternity services critical in primary health centres to save mothers and babies. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why is the presence of a midwife crucial at a primary health clinic or centre?

options.A: To manage hospital finances and procure medical equipment
options.B: To teach secondary school students anatomy and physiology
options.C: To perform complex caesarean sections independently in the clinic ward
options.D: To manage normal pregnancies and safely conduct routine deliveries

explanation: Midwives provide essential frontline care for pregnant women, spotting danger signs early and delivering babies safely. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h4)

question: What distinguishes a comprehensive health centre from a smaller primary health clinic?

options.A: It does not admit patients for observation
options.B: It only provides immunisation without antenatal care
options.C: It is located exclusively in national capital cities
options.D: Presence of a wider multidisciplinary team and minor surgical capacity

explanation: Comprehensive centres have advanced staff and facilities like operating rooms to handle more demanding primary cases. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h5)

question: What role do comprehensive health centres play in relation to smaller surrounding health posts?

options.A: They serve as administrative courts for health workers
options.B: They close down smaller health posts to centralize all patients
options.C: They compete with health posts for community immunisation funds
options.D: They act as referral receiving units for complicated cases

explanation: Smaller units send patients needing higher-level primary attention or minor surgery up to the comprehensive health centre. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which cadre of health workers forms the core backbone for maternal and child health services in primary facilities?
explanation: Midwives and nurses specialize in providing direct care to pregnant women, nursing mothers, and infants at the grassroots. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary responsibility of Community Health Extension Workers in a primary health facility?

options.A: Performing complex major neurosurgeries in the operating theatre
options.B: Handling international health policy and federal budgets
options.C: Providing basic general outpatient care and community health outreach
options.D: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs for regional distribution

explanation: Extension workers are trained to diagnose and treat common ailments and promote health education at the community level. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h6)

question: What crucial document must a midwife send along with a patient being referred to a secondary hospital?

options.A: A copy of the national health policy handbook
options.B: A personal diary of the midwife's daily routine
options.C: A receipt for community tax payment
options.D: A standardized referral note detailing clinical history and treatment given

explanation: A formal referral note ensures the receiving team knows what happened and what immediate care the patient received. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h7)

question: A woman at a primary health clinic develops severe postpartum hemorrhage that does not respond to initial uterotonics and uterine massage. What is the most appropriate immediate next step?

options.A: Perform major abdominal surgery on the clinic wooden examination couch
options.B: Discharge the patient home with advice to drink plenty of water
options.C: Stabilize, initiate IV access, and urgently refer the patient to a secondary facility
options.D: Wait patiently at the clinic overnight to see if bleeding stops on its own

explanation: Uncontrolled hemorrhage exceeds primary capability, requiring prompt stabilization and transfer to a higher-level hospital. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h7)
